extracted.intended_audience: Principal investigators, senior/key personnel, authorized organizational representatives, and sponsored-project offices preparing NSF proposals
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and mandatory requirements for preparing and submitting research and related proposals to the U.S. National Science Foundation, including formatting, required sections, certifications, disclosure rules, and special proposal types. Geared to ensuring proposals conform to the PAPPG (NSF 24-1) requirements and are not returned without review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conformance with Proposal Preparation Instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: All proposals must comply with the proposal preparation instructions contained in Part I of the PAPPG or the NSF Grants.gov Application Guide unless a written deviation authorization is received in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deviations require written authorization from the cognizant NSF Assistant Director/Office Head or designee; such authorization must be uploaded as a single-copy document and include the name, date, title of the NSF official, and the nature of the deviation. Except as authorized, NSF will not accept or will return without review proposals that are not consistent with these instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for Reasonable and Accessibility Accommodations
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals with disabilities who need reasonable accommodations as part of the proposal process or accessibility accommodations to access NSF systems must request them in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact the OECR Disability Program Manager (rarequest@nsf.gov) or NSF Section 508 Compliance Officer at least 30 calendar days prior to the proposal deadline (or 30 days in advance if no deadline). NSF may request medical documentation describing nature, severity, duration, activities limited, and why the accommodation is needed. Information is confidential; accommodations that impose undue hardship or fundamentally alter programs may be denied. Requests may not include personal use items or deadline extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preaward Disclosure Requirements (Senior/Key Personnel)
rubrics_metrics.description: All individuals designated as senior/key persons on a proposal must submit certain disclosure information to assist reviewers and program staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosures are provided through the Biographical Sketch, Current and Pending (Other) Support, and Collaborators & Other Affiliations documents. Individuals must certify that these documents are accurate, current, and complete and are required to update Current and Pending support prior to award; NSF may require updates prior to funding recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postaward Disclosure Requirements (Foreign Financial Support)
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions receiving NSF funding must disclose annually foreign financial support of $50,000 or more associated with a foreign country of concern, as required by the CHIPS and Science Act of 2022.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Chapter VII.D.3 for preparation and submission of the foreign financial disclosure report; additional postaward disclosure requirements are in Chapter IX.C.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for Violations of Pre- and Postaward Disclosure Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Violations of disclosure requirements may lead to criminal, civil, and/or administrative consequences and will be investigated by NSF OIG and others as warranted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Possible actions include non-acceptance or return of proposals, exclusion from performing work under an NSF award, ineligibility as an NSF reviewer, suspension/termination of awards, and placement in SAM or FAPIIS. NSF may consider harm, intent, knowledge of requirements, pattern vs isolated incident, self-disclosure, available policies/training, and other mitigating factors when determining consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal Pagination
rubrics_metrics.description: Research.gov will automatically paginate proposals; uploaded files should omit page numbering unless directed otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each uploaded section should leave out page numbering; Research.gov auto-pagination is relied upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Font, Spacing, and Margin Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals must use specified fonts/sizes, line density limits, margins at least one inch, and standard letter paper size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed fonts: Arial (not Arial Narrow), Courier New, Palatino Linotype (10 pt or larger); Times New Roman (11 pt or larger); Computer Modern family (11 pt or larger). A font under 10 pt may be used for formulas, figures, tables, captions, or special characters. No more than six lines of text per vertical inch. Margins >= 1 inch in all directions. Readability is paramount; noncompliance or use of smaller fonts to squeeze more text may be grounds for returning the proposal without review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page Formatting (Single-column recommended)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposers are strongly encouraged to use a standard, single-column format for text and to prioritize readability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of small fonts to gain advantage is prohibited; readability takes precedence over fitting more text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-Copy Documents (NSF Use Only)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain submitted documents are for "NSF Use Only" and are not provided to reviewers; these must be submitted in Research.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include Authorization to Deviate, List of Suggested Reviewers/Reviewers Not to Include, Proprietary or Privileged Information submissions, and proposal certifications provided by the organization. See Chapter II.D.1 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of Suggested Reviewers or Reviewers Not to Include (optional)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposers may optionally include a list of suggested reviewers and/or a list of persons they prefer not to review the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include reviewer name, email address, and organizational affiliation. Suggestions are optional and the cognizant Program Officer decides whether to use them and may contact the proposer for more information. See Exhibit II-2 for conflicts of interest guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proprietary or Privileged Information Submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructions exist for submission of proprietary or privileged information when applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Chapter II.E.1 and Chapter II.B for detailed instructions and how single-copy handling applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized Organizational Representative (AOR) Responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: An AOR must use the authorized organizational representative function to sign and submit the proposal and complete required NSF-specific certifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposing organization is responsible to ensure only properly authorized individuals complete submission. Government-wide certifications and representations are provided in SAM annually; certain certifications must be submitted with the proposal via Research.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification: AOR or Individual Proposer Accuracy and Compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The AOR must certify accuracy and completeness of statements in the proposal and agree that the organization will comply with award terms and conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a required NSF-specific certification submitted by the AOR with the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification: Conflict of Interest (Organization)
rubrics_metrics.description: The AOR must certify that the organization has a written conflict of interest (COI) policy, has enforced it, and that required financial disclosures were made and conflicts managed appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conflicts that cannot be satisfactorily managed must be disclosed to NSF via electronic systems. See Chapter IX.A for COI provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification: Flood Hazard Insurance
rubrics_metrics.description: AORs for recipients in FEMA-designated special flood hazard areas must certify that adequate flood insurance has been or will be obtained in certain circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies for awards for construction of a building/facility and for other awards when more than $25,000 is budgeted for repair/alteration/construction. Proposers should contact local authorities or federally-insured financial institutions to determine flood hazard status and insurance availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification: Responsible and Ethical Conduct of Research (RECR)
rubrics_metrics.description: The AOR must certify that the institution has a plan to provide appropriate training and oversight in RECR for undergraduate students, graduate students, postdocs, faculty, and other senior/key personnel who will be supported by NSF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training plans need not be included in proposals but may be reviewed upon request. NSF provides resources via the Online Ethics Center for S&E.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification: Organizational Support
rubrics_metrics.description: The AOR must certify that the organization provides the organizational support described in the proposal, including support for broader impacts and intellectual merit activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certification required by Section 526 of the America COMPETES Reauthorization Act of 2010; organizational support must be available as described in the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification: Dual Use Research of Concern (DURC)
rubrics_metrics.description: The AOR must certify that the organization will be or is in compliance with the U.S. Government Policy for Institutional Oversight of Life Sciences DURC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This certification is required to ensure institutional oversight for potential dual use life sciences research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification: William M. (Mac) Thornberry NDAA (Section 223)
rubrics_metrics.description: The AOR must certify that each individual identified as senior/key person has been made aware of the certification requirements in Section 223(a)(1) of the NDAA (42 U.S.C. § 6605(a)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Senior/key persons must certify accuracy of Biographical Sketch and Current and Pending Support in SciENcv and update disclosures as required; false representations may incur legal penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification: Safe and Inclusive Working Environments for Off-Campus/Off-Site Research
rubrics_metrics.description: For proposals that include off-campus or off-site research, the AOR must certify the organization has a plan in place for safe and inclusive working environments for this proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Chapter II.E.9 for additional information; certification requirement applies when proposing off-campus/ off-site data collection or fieldwork.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification: Malign Foreign Talent Recruitment Programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Section 10632 of the CHIPS and Science Act, the AOR must certify that senior/key personnel have complied with responsibility to certify that the individual is not a party to a malign foreign talent recruitment program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individuals must certify prior to proposal submission and annually thereafter during the award. False representations can lead to prosecution under various statutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission Restrictions for Former NSF Staff
rubrics_metrics.description: For one year after separation, former NSF employees or IPAs must communicate with NSF through a 'substitute negotiator' and proposals listing such former staff as PI/co-PI will not be processed unless a substitute negotiator is designated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substitute negotiator must be from the same organization as the PI/co-PI; documentation designating substitute negotiator should be uploaded as a single-copy document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required Sections of a Full Research Proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: A full research proposal must contain: Cover Sheet, Project Summary, Table of Contents, Project Description, References Cited, Budget and Budget Justification, Facilities, Equipment and Other Resources, Senior/Key Personnel Documents (Biographical Sketches; Current and Pending Support; Collaborators & Other Affiliations; Synergistic Activities), and Special Information and Supplementary Documentation (e.g., Mentoring Plan, Data Management and Sharing Plan).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to submit required sections will result in the proposal not being accepted or being returned without review. Some proposal types have deviating requirements; see Chapter II.F for other types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover Sheet: Requested Start Date and Proposal Duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Requested duration should be consistent with the nature and complexity of the activity; NSF encourages requests of 3–5 years when necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requested start date should allow at least six months for NSF review, processing, and decision. PIs should consult their SPO for unusual situations. Requests for specific start dates may not be met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover Sheet: Organizational and Submission Identifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Awardee organization name, address, NSF organization code, UEI, and EIN/TIN are derived from organizational profile or SAM; organizations must identify their status by checking applicable boxes (e.g., for-profit, small business, minority-owned, woman-owned).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary Place of Performance defaults to organization's address; if different, provide primary site info. For research infrastructure that is mobile/distributed, provide primary site or HQ. See Chapter I.E for foreign organization funding rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Summary Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Summary must be no more than one page and include an overview, a statement on intellectual merit, and a statement on broader impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overview should describe the activity if funded and state objectives and methods. Intellectual merit describes potential to advance knowledge. Broader impacts describe potential societal benefits. Summary should be informative to peers and, where possible, understandable to a broad scientific audience; it should not be an abstract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Description Content
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Description must provide a clear statement of the work, including objectives, expected significance, relationship to the state of knowledge, plan of work (including methods), and justification of approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address what you want to do, why, how you plan to do it, how you'll know if successful, and potential benefits. Must include a separate section labeled 'Broader Impacts' as its own heading. Plans for data management and sharing belong in the Special Information section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Description Page Limitation and URL Prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Description (including Results from Prior NSF Support) may not exceed 15 pages; Results from Prior NSF Support is limited to five pages. URLs must not be used in the Project Description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visual materials are included in the 15-page limit. URLs are prohibited because they can circumvent page limits and may not be accessible or stable for reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broader Impacts Content and Examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Broader Impacts must describe how the proposed activity benefits society and contributes to desired societal outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include full participation of underrepresented groups, improved STEM education, increased public scientific literacy, improved well-being, a diverse STEM workforce, partnerships between academia and industry, improved national security, increased economic competitiveness, informing public policy, and enhancing research/education infrastructure. These examples are illustrative, not prescriptive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results from Prior NSF Support (RPS)
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicable, proposers must include Results from Prior NSF Support as part of the Project Description, limited to five pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RPS should describe relevant prior NSF-funded work, outcomes, and how those results inform the current proposal. This section is counted within the 15-page Project Description limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Budget Justification Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals must include a Budget and Budget Justification detailing requested funds and justification across required cost categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget must cover Salaries and Wages, Fringe Benefits, Equipment, Travel (domestic and foreign), Participant Support, Other Direct Costs (materials, publication, consultants, computer services, subawards, etc.), Total Direct Costs, Indirect Costs, Fees (if applicable), Amount of This Request, and Cost Sharing (if applicable). Budget Justification should explain and justify each requested cost including basis for amounts, and meet any solicitation-specific directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salaries and Wages Policies (Senior/Key and Administrative/Clerical)
rubrics_metrics.description: Salaries for senior/key personnel and administrative/clerical positions must follow NSF policy regarding when such costs are allowable as direct charges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative/clerical salaries are normally treated as indirect costs unless specific conditions are met to charge them directly. Senior/key personnel effort commitments and treatment must be consistent with NSF policies; see detailed policy sections in the PAPPG.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fringe Benefits, Equipment, Travel, and Participant Support Cost Policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowable treatment and documentation of fringe benefits, equipment purchases, travel (domestic and foreign), and participant support costs are governed by PAPPG instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foreign travel has special requirements and restrictions (see Chapter XI.F/footnotes). Participant support costs should be budgeted and documented according to solicitation and PAPPG guidance. Certain travel or equipment items may have additional agency restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Direct Costs Categories and Guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Other Direct Costs include materials and supplies (including computing devices), publication/documentation/dissemination costs, consultant services, computer services, subawards, and other direct expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each category has specific allowability and justification expectations. For example, data deposit or curation costs are allowable; subawards must be characterized by substance over nomenclature. Detailed instructions and definitions are in PAPPG sections referenced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable and Unallowable Costs (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: PAPPG lists categories of costs that are not allowable or are restricted, including entertainment, certain meals/coffee breaks, alcoholic beverages, home office workspace, and prohibited telecommunications/video surveillance equipment/services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposers must follow allowability rules and prohibitions; see PAPPG subsections for specifics (e.g., prohibition on certain telecom equipment). Inclusion of unallowable items may lead to budget disallowance or proposal rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities, Equipment, and Other Resources Section
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposers must provide a Facilities, Equipment and Other Resources section describing institutional resources available to the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This section documents available infrastructure and support but is not a budget; it helps reviewers and NSF assess the institutional environment and feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical Sketches and Senior/Key Personnel Documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Biographical Sketch(es) must be provided for senior/key personnel (and other personnel when required) following NSF format and requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different formats may apply for equipment proposals vs standard proposals; biographical sketches must include required elements and certifications of accuracy. Senior/key personnel must certify information prior to proposal submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Current and Pending (Other) Support Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Senior/key personnel must submit Current and Pending (Other) Support information disclosing all current and pending support that is relevant to the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This information must be accurate and up-to-date; individuals certify its accuracy. NSF may require updates prior to award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborators & Other Affiliations Disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposers must provide Collaborators & Other Affiliations information to help identify potential conflicts of interest and reviewer selection issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This information is used by NSF to manage conflicts and reviewer assignments; see Chapter II.D.1 for submission details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synergistic Activities Documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Synergistic activities of senior/key personnel should be documented as required in the biographical sketch format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These activities demonstrate broader professional contributions and engagements; follow NSF biographical sketch instructions for content and length.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentoring Plan Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A mentoring plan is required in certain proposals that support postdoctoral researchers and similar personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The mentoring plan must be included in the Special Information and Supplementary Documentation section; for collaboratively submitted projects and those with subawards, one unified mentoring plan suffices for the entire project. In situations where a postdoc functions as senior/key personnel, a mentoring plan may not be required (see footnotes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Management and Sharing Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals must include plans for management and sharing of data and research products in the Special Information and Supplementary Documentation section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plans should address preservation, documentation, and sharing of data, samples, physical collections, curriculum materials, and other related products. Data deposit and curation costs may be budgeted where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of Collaboration (Documentation of Collaborative Arrangements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Collaborative arrangements of significance should be documented through Letters of Collaboration uploaded in the supplementary documentation section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters should describe the nature of the collaboration and commitments but should not be used to circumvent page limits or become single-copy-only content unless specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Environmental Statutes and Compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals involving environmental impacts must address applicable federal environmental statutes and compliance requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific documentation and processing instructions are provided in the PAPPG and may be required as supplementary materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logistical Requirements and Field Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: When research requires fieldwork or significant logistical support, proposers must include a logistical/field plan in the Special Information section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The plan should describe field safety, access, timelines, transportation, housing, and other logistics necessary for review of feasibility and risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research in Registered Historic Places
rubrics_metrics.description: If research is conducted in locations that are designated or eligible as Registered Historic Places, proposers must provide required justification/documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Chapter II.D.2.i(vii) for instructions and required materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Involving Genetically Engineered Organisms and DURC
rubrics_metrics.description: Research involving genetically engineered organisms, potential DURC, or other life-science dual-use concerns must include appropriate documentation and institutional oversight plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Chapter II.E.6 and related policy sections; include certifications and compliance information as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation Regarding Human Subjects, Hazardous Materials, Live Vertebrate Animals, or Endangered Species
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals involving human subjects, hazardous materials, live vertebrate animals, or endangered species must include required supplemental documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplemental instructions and forms are specified in the PAPPG (e.g., animal care forms, IRB documentation) and must be provided where applicable; failure to include required documentation can result in non-acceptance or return.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Components in New Proposals or Requests for Supplemental Funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain new proposals or supplement requests have special components or processing requirements that must be included as described in PAPPG.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposers should consult the relevant PAPPG subsections for details on additional components required for special solicitations or supplement types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Processing Instructions (including Proprietary Information Handling)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some proposals require special processing (e.g., proprietary information review) and must follow designated submission routes and single-copy handling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the instructions in the PAPPG for marking and submitting proprietary/privileged information and other items requiring single-copy handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative Proposals Submission Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Collaborative proposals (single organization vs multiple organizations) have particular preparation and submission instructions that must be followed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed collaborative proposal preparation steps are in Research.gov and PAPPG Chapter II.E. Single unified components (e.g., mentoring plan) may cover the entire collaborative project where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposals Involving Live Vertebrate Animals
rubrics_metrics.description: If the proposal includes live vertebrate animals, supplemental information and compliance documentation are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplemental info requirements and approved formats are in Chapter II.E.4 and referenced guidelines (e.g., species-specific guidelines). Failure to include required documentation may result in non-acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposals Involving Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals involving human subjects require supplemental documentation and compliance with human subjects protections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include IRB documentation or justification and follow Chapter II.E.5 instructions; human subjects work cannot proceed without required approvals and documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential Life Sciences Dual Use Research of Concern (DURC) Identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposers must identify potential life sciences DURC and provide required oversight information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Chapters II.E.6 and XI.B.5 for identification and institutional oversight expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Projects Requiring Advanced Computing Resources, Data, and Analysis Capabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals needing significant advanced computing resources or specialized data/analysis support should follow guidance for describing needs and may need to contact relevant programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposers are encouraged to discuss resource availability and requirements with program officers prior to submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Activities and Foreign Organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals with international activities must list primary countries on the Cover Sheet; proposals that include funding to a foreign organization, foreign individual, or international branch campus require explanations/justification in the Project Description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If international conference locations are unknown, enter 'Worldwide'. Additional requirements apply to funding foreign organizations/individuals (see Chapter I.E).

rubrics_metrics.name: Safe and Inclusive Working Environments for Off-Campus or Off-Site Research (AOR Certification)
rubrics_metrics.description: For proposals proposing off-campus/off-site research, the AOR must certify that the organization has a plan in place regarding safe and inclusive working environments for this proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Chapter II.E.9 for required plan elements and certification procedures; applies to fieldwork, vessel/aircraft research, and similar activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seeking and Obtaining Tribal Nation Approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals that may impact Tribal resources or interests should seek and obtain Tribal Nation approval where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on seeking Tribal Nation approval procedures and documentation is provided in the PAPPG; proposers should plan early and include relevant documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of Proposals with Deviating Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain proposal types (Planning, RAPID, EAGER, RAISE, GOALI, Ideas Lab, FASED, Conference, Equipment, Travel, Center, Research Infrastructure, Postdoctoral Fellowship, CLB supplements, ROA-PUI supplements) have specific instructions that may deviate from the standard content requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposers must consult Chapter II.F for type-specific preparation rules and follow solicitation-specific guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career-Life Balance (CLB) Supplemental Funding Requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients of research awards, postdoctoral fellowships (institutional), or GRFP recipients may request CLB supplemental funding to support personnel to sustain research during family leave situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CLB supplements may fund up to six months of salary/stipend support (max $30,000 direct salary/stipend) plus fringe and F&A (not tuition). Requests must be submitted via Research.gov 'Supplemental Funding Request', adequately justified, may take up to two months or more to process, and usually reviewed internally unless external review is needed. Requests must specify it's a CLB request, describe how the replacement will sustain research, provide a budget and justification, identify period of performance, include an organizational certification statement (specified language), GRFP requests must include faculty advisor letter, and must not include privacy-related reasons for leave.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Opportunity Supplemental Funding Requests for Primarily Undergraduate Institutions (ROA-PUI)
rubrics_metrics.description: ROA-PUI supplements enable eligible PUI faculty to visit another NSF-supported institution to pursue collaborative research and must meet eligibility and documentation requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility: host or home organization must be an eligible PUI (accredited U.S. IHE with main campus in U.S.; awarded 20 or fewer PhD/D.Sci degrees in NSF fields in the combined previous two academic years). Submission must be by host institution using Research.gov Supplemental Funding Request and include summary of proposed work, budget and justification, biographical sketch and Current & Pending support for the PUI faculty, proposed period (typically 2–12 months), and a signed 'Certification of ROA-PUI Eligibility' on institutional letterhead executed by the PUI AOR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal Preparation Checklist and Exhibits
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Exhibit II-1 Proposal Preparation Checklist and supporting exhibits (Exhibit II-2 Potentially Disqualifying Conflicts of Interest; Exhibit II-3 Definitions of Categories of Personnel) to assist in administrative review before submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The checklist highlights critical items but is not an all-inclusive repetition of required contents. Proposers are strongly encouraged to perform an administrative review prior to submission. Noncompliance may cause return without review.
